title: Embedding billing: velocity-smoothing ladder, burst credits, and QSA intake
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers are requesting smoother per-vector billing that avoids large monthly bill spikes from short bursts of high QPS (eg. indexing jobs, model warm-ups) while preserving clear marginal pricing for cost forecasting. Current per-vector and batch discounts create discontinuities and edge cases that frustrate finance and procurement (large one-time rerank jobs cause unexpectedly high charges).

Goal: Design and validate a pricing architecture that 1) introduces a velocity-smoothing ladder for per-vector units (time-decayed effective unit rates), 2) offers an explicit burst credit mechanism for one-off high-throughput events, and 3) preserves simple visibility for QSA and contract flows.

Scope: Pricing change applies to embeddings and rerank endpoints; does not change API surface. Work includes: product proposal, pricing model simulation, QSA/security questionnaire updates, billing-side implementation requirements, API docs updates, and enterprise sales playbook collateral.
acceptance_criteria: Simulated customer invoice examples show <= 20% month-over-month variance for common burst patterns compared to current pricing
Billing pipeline design doc and PRD reviewed by Billing Infra and Finance
QSA package updated with clear non-repudiation and data handling language and accepted by Security (TODO: sign-off date)
Pilot agreement template and pricing sheet for early enterprise trials produced
Telemetry signal definitions and dashboards for tracking per-customer burst credit consumption live in Console
notes: Design constraint: must be expressible as line items in customer invoices and compatible with existing per-token/per-embed metering hooks
Trade-off: aggressive smoothing reduces customer surprise but shifts short-term revenue recognition; Finance prefers conservative ramp
Legal input requested on how to describe burst credits vs prepaid commit in customer contracts
